clue.text: Came about having reversed large car into aromatic plant

indicators.note: about means the word Came is wrapped around the other piece, its letters split to take it in
reversed says the word for the large car is read from back to front

parts.note: a limo, short for limousine, is a large car

explanation.surface: Someone drove their limousine backwards into a fragrant herb bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Came about' looks like 'happened', but CAME is the outer piece; 'reversed' makes OMIL, and 'about' wraps CAME round it.
explanation.definitionFit: This daisy-like herb, used for soothing tea, has a strong sweet scent.

clue.text: Box for first Christmas present

indicators.note: first asks for only the opening letter of the word Christmas

parts.note: to offer is to present, as in present a gift

explanation.surface: A box given as the first Christmas present.
explanation.definitionFit: A strongbox or chest for valuables is a box.

clue.text: Mixture doctor uses to make a frothy cream

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a common abbreviation for a doctor

indicators.note: Mixture tells us the letters of uses are jumbled together into a new order

explanation.surface: A doctor uses a mixture to whip up a frothy cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mixture' reorders USES as USSE; MO is a standard abbreviation for a medical officer.
explanation.definitionFit: This light whipped dessert or foamy preparation is an airy cream.

clue.text: It bites some amid general populous

indicators.note: some means only part of the following words is taken, a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: Something that bites is found among the general populace.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'amid general'; 'populous' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This tiny fly delivers itchy bites, notoriously in the Scottish Highlands.

clue.text: French articles get dry here

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article, the
un is the French masculine indefinite article, a
taken as written

explanation.surface: Clothes and other articles are taken somewhere to be dried.
explanation.walkthrough: 'articles' does double duty in the surface: grammatical words in the wordplay, clothing in the whole reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Washed clothing is dried in a room or business set aside for washing.

clue.text: Force the family

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to stretch or exert effort; the other is a line of descent or stock, as in a strain of a breed.

clue.text: Ketch Enid used when it got murky

indicators.note: used here means put to work in a different way, so the letters of Ketch Enid are rearranged

explanation.surface: Enid used her ketch when the weather turned murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used' is a loose anagram signal: the letters are re-used in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid or fog that has become denser has grown cloudy and murky.

clue.text: Given key, fellows are fit and co-operative

parts.note: A is a musical key
men are fellows
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: Men in the right key prove fit and willing to work together.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone willing to go along with a plan is tractable and co-operative.

clue.text: An awful crisis when bloomers are made

indicators.note: awful suggests the letters of An crisis are in a terrible mess and need rearranging

explanation.surface: Making a mistake turns into an awful crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomers' suggests blunders or underwear, but here means flowering plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Daffodils and their kin are flowers, things that bloom.

clue.text: Discovered to be away from home

explanation.walkthrough: Someone who called while you were not home 'found you out'.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is exposed or detected; the other is a caller learning you were not in.

clue.text: Article in ship of the line

indicators.note: in means the article's letter goes inside the word for the ship

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: An article about a ship of the line, a naval warship.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear describes anything arranged along or relating to a straight stroke.

clue.text: A bird found at sea?

explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, the British women's navy.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a tiny brown songbird; the other is a woman serving in the British navy.

clue.text: There's no point on TV soap coming to a conclusion during the holiday

definitions.text: There's no point on TV soap

indicators.note: during says one piece sits inside the word for the holiday

parts.note: Easter is a spring holiday
a conclusion is an end

explanation.surface: Viewers of a TV soap reach its conclusion over the holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: EastEnders is a long-running BBC soap set in London's East End; take off its S (a compass point, 'no point') to get one resident.
explanation.definitionFit: A resident of London's East End, as in the soap's title, minus its final compass point.

clue.text: Of uniform colour

parts.note: reads like 'all one shade', but means the dull brownish shade of army uniforms

explanation.definitionFit: This dusty brownish-green is the traditional shade of military dress.

clue.text: A method which is off

parts.note: a way is a method

explanation.surface: A method that is off.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone off on holiday is absent, not here.

clue.text: Bill in the heather? No. the opposite, happily

indicators.note: in, turned round by 'No. the opposite', means the heather goes inside the name for Bill

parts.note: Willy, like Bill, is short for William
ling is a common heather

explanation.surface: Is Bill hiding in the heather? No, quite the reverse, and gladly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No. the opposite' flips the containment the clue first states, so the heather sits inside the name rather than the name in the heather.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something gladly and without reluctance is doing it readily and with pleasure.

clue.text: No French mathematical sign should cause bewilderment

parts.note: non is French for no
plus is the + sign in arithmetic

explanation.surface: A French refusal to use a maths sign baffles everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: To baffle someone completely is to bewilder them.

clue.text: Olga paid for treatment to painful feet

indicators.note: treatment means the letters of Olga paid are worked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Olga paid for treatment to her painful feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'treatment' is the anagram signal, reworking OLGA PAID.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term, from Greek for foot and pain, names aching feet.

clue.text: Places ship's company so as to prevent movement

definitions.note: a phrase describing the purpose of the noun answer

parts.note: sets means places, puts down
a crew is the company of a ship

explanation.surface: Someone positions the ship's company to keep it from moving.
explanation.definitionFit: This small headless screw holds one part fast against another so it cannot slip.

clue.text: Cover work about Ravel composition

indicators.note: about means the word for work is placed around the other letters

parts.note: op, short for opus, is a musical work

indicators.note: composition means the letters of Ravel are composed into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A cover version of a piece about a work by Ravel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' reorders RAVEL as VERLA; a musical work as OP (opus) is a standard abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To extend over part of something is to partly cover it.

clue.text: Staff appointment?

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a pole or upright stick; the other is a job or position held.

clue.text: Indicates approval when boy returns carrying old coin

indicators.note: carrying means the reversed boy holds the coin inside it
returns says the word for boy is read backwards

parts.note: a son is a boy
d stood for the old British penny, from Latin denarius

explanation.surface: A father approves when his son comes home with an old coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returns' turns SON into NOS, which carries D: NO D S.
explanation.definitionFit: Bobbing the head shows agreement or assent.

clue.text: Makes rather a fuss when legs are wobbly after knocking back gin!

indicators.note: after places the wobbly legs behind the reversed gin
knocking back, like downing a drink, means the gin is turned backwards

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: are wobbly means the letters of legs are unsteady and rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone fusses about wobbly legs after downing a gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking back' (downing a drink) makes NIG; 'are wobbly' makes GLES, set 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: To nag or carp over trifles is to fuss pettily.

clue.text: Mutual confusion over German letter

indicators.note: confusion says the letters of Mutual are confused into a new order

explanation.surface: Mutual confusion over a letter written in German.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-dot mark over a vowel, as in ü, is characteristic of written German.

clue.text: Cornered fish perhaps

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is having corners or slanting; the other is tried to catch with rod and line.

clue.text: Some bananas sailors brought from a South American palm

definitions.text: brought from a South American palm

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Sailors brought back some bananas from South America.
explanation.definitionFit: The açaí palm of Brazil yields a berry used in drinks and food.

clue.text: Cruelly maligns an operative of the railways

indicators.note: Cruelly suggests the letters of maligns are cruelly twisted out of shape

explanation.surface: Someone cruelly slanders a railway worker.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway worker who operates the points and signals from a box.

clue.text: Doctor takes the beer round at a rather slow pace, perhaps

indicators.note: round means the beer goes around the doctor's letters

parts.note: ale is beer
MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification

explanation.surface: A doctor carries the beer round at a leisurely pace.
explanation.definitionFit: A leisurely stroll is a gentle walking gait.

clue.text: Silver gear shift to put in car

indicators.note: to put in means the silver goes inside the shifted gear
shift means the letters of gear are moved into a new order

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Putting a car into gear and shifting it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shift' turns GEAR into GARE; AG goes 'in': GAR + AG + E.
explanation.definitionFit: A building where a motor vehicle is kept or serviced.

clue.text: Sounds like the caddy's job, making difficult tack

indicators.note: Sounds like says the phrase for the caddy's task is said aloud, near enough

parts.note: a golf caddy's work is to haul clubs: a clubs-haul

explanation.surface: A golf caddy's work is hard going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sounds like' gives 'clubs haul', said quickly. To clubhaul is to tack a sailing ship by dropping the lee anchor to swing her round, an emergency manoeuvre off a lee shore.
explanation.definitionFit: This emergency manoeuvre swings a ship onto a new heading in tight conditions.

clue.text: Ever saw lay-about?

indicators.note: about here means the letters of saw lay are turned about into a different order

explanation.surface: Have you ever seen such a layabout?
explanation.walkthrough: 'lay-about' looks like one idle person, but splits so that 'about' becomes the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Forever, at all times, is what both words mean.

clue.text: Agreed to use end seats

indicators.note: use means the letters of end seats are put to use in another order

explanation.surface: Someone agreed to take the seats at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying yes to a proposal is consenting to it.
